npcs.name: Maren Hale
npcs.idle: Have you seen a young man with a lantern and more nerve than sense? No? Then never mind me.

npcs.name: Hob Tanner
npcs.idle: I'm just here. Minding my business. Like a sensible man.

npcs.name: Brother Eadric
npcs.idle: Walk softly. Mithra's faithful have not stopped praying down here - they have only stopped breathing.

npcs.name: Ysolde Marchant
npcs.idle: Mind the loom. Everything else in this house is already unravelling.

npcs.name: Gerrit the Woodcutter
npcs.idle: Keep your voice down. They sing at night, up the hill, and I'd sooner they didn't hear us.

npcs.name: Tamsin
npcs.idle: Grandad says faeries can't count past three. I can count to a hundred. That's why I'm in charge.

npcs.name: Warden Hollis
npcs.idle: Camelot's walls are an hour's walk. You'd think that would keep the trouble off. It doesn't.

npcs.name: Goodwife Ada
npcs.idle: Three lambs this week. Three. The wolves never came this close when the King was alive.

npcs.name: Bran the Miller
npcs.idle: The wheel's stopped. You hear that? Nothing. That's my living, not turning.

npcs.name: Reeve Tobias
npcs.idle: Half the harvest's in, the other half's walking off into the hills on little green legs.

npcs.name: Forester Odo
npcs.idle: These were the King's woods. They still are, as far as I'm concerned.

npcs.name: Gronyr the Farmer
npcs.idle: My grandfather's grandfather ploughed this field. The ants say otherwise.

npcs.name: Watch-Captain Elidyr
npcs.idle: Every road to Camelot is my road. I'd like them back.

npcs.name: Sir Bedwyr
npcs.idle: I sat three places down from Sir Kay. He never let me forget it. Now there's no one to forget it to.

npcs.name: Brother Idris
npcs.idle: I bless the dead in the barrow fields every Sunday. This year they've started answering.

npcs.name: Sage Tegid
npcs.idle: Old Rome built that tomb for Mithras. Old Rome didn't build it to be used by these people.

npcs.name: Lady Enid
npcs.idle: The door to Darkness Falls is held. Mostly. Things get round it.

npcs.name: Sir Barwick
npcs.idle: Barwick. Not Berwick. I've corrected three demons on it.

quests.title: What the Tomb Keeps
quests.offer:
Please - a moment. My brother Caddoc went off four nights ago with a lantern, a shovel and a map he swore was worth a fortune. He said he'd be back by market day. Market day was yesterday.

He's reckless, not stupid. Mostly. His friend [Hob] knows more than he lets on. Will you [look for him]? I'd go myself, but someone has to keep our mother from going after him.

topics.Hob: Hob Tanner. They go everywhere together - or did. Hob's been jumping at shadows since Caddoc left. He's by the east road, pretending to work.

quests.summary: Maren Hale's brother Caddoc went treasure hunting four nights ago and never came home.

steps.goal: Ask Hob Tanner where Caddoc went
steps.say: Maren sent you? Gods. All right. We bought the map off a pedlar in Ludlow - an old Mithran thing, he said, from the tomb in the eastern hills. Caddoc was set on it. I went with him as far as the [barrows] and then I... I came back. I'm not proud of it.

steps.goal: Find Caddoc's camp near the old tomb in the eastern hills

clue.name: a cold campfire and a bedroll

steps.text: The fire is days cold. His bedroll is still here, and beside it, scratched into a stone: 'Gone below. Back by dark.' He never came back for the bedroll.

steps.goal: Go into the Tomb of Mithra and look for anyone who saw him
steps.say:
A young man with a lantern? Yes. He went past me singing, if you can believe it. I warned him the deeper halls belong to the cult - the ones who still keep Mithra's rites over the dead. He laughed and said he'd be quick.

That was four days ago. If you go after him, look where they bring their [offerings].

steps.goal: Search the cult's offering halls deep in the tomb
steps.text: Caddoc's lantern, dented and dark. The map is folded inside it, and on the back, in a shaking hand: 'They are not dead. They are not dead. They want me to stay.'

steps.goal: Find what became of Caddoc
steps.text: As he falls, the thing that was Caddoc Hale stills. For a heartbeat his eyes are his own. 'Tell Maren,' he whispers, 'I'm sorry. Tell her I found something after all.'

stages.name: The Unquiet Offering
stages.announce: Something shambles out of the dark with a familiar face. The cult's whispering rises: another offering, another servant.
stages.fail: You fall back into the tunnels.

steps.goal: Return to Maren Hale in Cotswold
steps.text: Maren sees your face before you say a word.

steps.goal: Tell Maren what you found
steps.say:
You found him. I can see it. Don't - just tell me. Was it quick? Is he... is he coming home?

You could tell her [the truth]. Or you could [spare her], and tell her he went south to find work.

options.say:
...Raised. By those things. And you gave him rest.

Then he isn't down there in the dark any more. That's - that's something. Thank you for not lying to me. I think I'd have known.

South? To work? Caddoc?

Then he's alive. He's alive and he's a fool, and one day he'll walk through that door with a story. I'll keep his supper warm. Thank you. Thank you.

truth.text: Our father's ring was meant to go to Caddoc. He'd want it to go to someone brave. And his lantern - keep that too. He'd like it being carried somewhere.

mercy.text: Here - for your trouble. It's not much. When he comes back, I'll tell him who to thank.

quests.title: The Pilgrim's Letters
quests.offer:
My son Elric went north with a band of pilgrims a month ago. Holy men, he said - dwarves, of all things, from some deep hall. His first letters were full of hymns. The last one... the last one called me 'the woman who raised me' and told me to burn my [loom].

I'm a weaver. I don't know how to go and fetch a boy back from a faith. But you might. Will you [find him]?

topics.loom: His father built it. Elric used to sleep under it when he was small. Now he writes that it's 'a chain of the world above'. He's twenty. He doesn't know what a chain is.

quests.summary: Ysolde Marchant's son Elric followed a band of dwarven 'pilgrims' north, and his letters have stopped sounding like him.

steps.goal: Follow the old north road out of Cotswold
steps.text: At the waystone, the road's mud holds a dozen sets of heavy boots - short strides, all in step - and the drag-marks of a cart. Smoke rises from a woodcutter's hut to the east.

steps.goal: Ask the woodcutter about the pilgrims
steps.say:
Pilgrims? Is that what they call themselves? Short fellows in grey, aye, and a lot of tall young folk walking with them like sleepwalkers. They camp up the hill by the old stones and they sing till dawn. Same three notes. My dog won't go near.

The young ones throw away everything they brought - I've found purses, boots, [letters] in the bracken.

steps.goal: Search the bracken below the pilgrims' camp
steps.text: Letters, dozens of them, never sent. One in Elric's hand, half-finished: 'Mother - I can't remember the colour of the loom. The Brothers say that's good. Why does it feel like drowning?'

steps.goal: Bring Elric back to himself - and out of the camp
steps.text: Elric stares at the letter in his own hand for a long time. Then he asks, very quietly, whether the loom is still there.

stages.name: Three Notes
stages.objective: Keep Elric alive while he wakes
stages.announce: You read Elric his own words. He blinks - and the singing stops. Every grey robe turns towards him.
stages.thanks: I... I know you. No. I know the letter. Who are you?
stages.fail: Elric is dragged back into the singing.

stages.name: The Deep Hall's Voice
stages.objective: Silence the priest who leads the singing
stages.announce: A dwarf in grey steps out of the stones, still humming the three notes. 'The boy is ours. The world above is a lie. Come below.'

boss.name: Brother Thrangar of the Deep Hall

stages.fail: The hymn swells and you are driven off the hill.

steps.goal: Bring word to Ysolde in Cotswold
steps.text: Elric took the long way home - through every field he used to play in, he said. He's there before you.

steps.goal: Speak with Ysolde
steps.say: He walked in and sat down under the loom like he was six years old. He hasn't said much. He keeps touching the threads.

home.text: His father made this loom. I'd like you to have something from it - I wove this the night you left, hoping. Take whichever suits you.

quests.title: The Bell-Wether's Price
quests.offer:
You're a hero, aren't you? You've got a sword and everything. The faeries took Grandad's silver pipe - the one he plays for the sheep - and now the sheep won't come home and Grandad sits by the fire doing nothing.

They live by the [faerie ring] in the woods north of the lake. Will you [get it back]? I'd do it but I'm eight.

topics.faerie ring: North of the big lake with the lady in it. Don't talk to the lady. Grandad says she's for kings.

quests.summary: Little Tamsin's grandfather's silver pipe was stolen by the faeries north of the lake.

steps.goal: Find the faerie ring north of the lake
steps.text: Tiny laughter all around you, and the tinkle of a dozen stolen bells. Something throws an acorn at your head.

steps.goal: Teach the mischief-makers some manners
steps.text: The giggling stops. A faerie in a coat of bluebells drifts down to look at you, clearly unimpressed.

steps.goal: Speak with whoever rules this ring
Bargain with Wren for the silver pipe
steps.say:
You've been terribly rude to my cousins. Still, you came all this way for a little pipe. The Bell-Wether likes it - it plays the sheep-song, and sheep-songs are rare.

I could simply [return] it, since you've proved so tiresome. Or we could [bargain]: let us keep it, and the Bell-Wether will owe you a favour. Faerie favours are worth a great deal more than pipes.

options.say: Oh, very well. Take your pipe. Tell the shepherd his sheep-song is lovely and that he plays it flat.
Wise. Hold out your hand - there. Something to remember us by. The shepherd will find other songs. Probably.

steps.goal: Bring the silver pipe home to Tamsin
steps.say: You got it! You actually got it! Grandad! GRANDAD! Listen - he's playing - and the sheep are coming! Look at them all!

steps.goal: Tell Tamsin what you agreed with the faeries
steps.say:
They're keeping it? For a FAVOUR? That's not fair. That's... that's a grown-up thing to do.

...Grandad says it's all right. He says he'll whittle a new one. He says faeries keep their promises better than most people. I'm still cross.

returned.text: Grandad says to give you this - he says it's for luck, and that you'll need it more than he does now.

bargained.text: ...You can have this. Grandad says. Hmph.

quests.title: Wolves at the Fold
quests.offer:
Three lambs this week. The grey wolves come down off the downs at dusk and take them right out of the fold, bold as you like.

Warden Hollis says he can't spare a man. Will you [watch the fold] tonight? Thin the pups out on the fields and follow them home.
quests.summary: Grey wolves are taking Goodwife Ada's lambs from the fold outside Cotswold.

steps.goal: Thin out the wolf pups on the fields about 150 m east of Goodwife Ada
Follow the tracks north to the wolves' den

clue.name: a den under a fallen oak

steps.text: Bones. Lots of them, and fresh. And a tuft of grey fur on the root - the old she-wolf's, by the size of it.

steps.goal: Drive off the old she-wolf
steps.text: The she-wolf drops at the mouth of her den. The downs go quiet.

stages.name: Old Greymuzzle
stages.announce: A grey wolf as big as a pony comes out of the dark under the oak, and she isn't afraid of you.

steps.goal: Tell Goodwife Ada
steps.say:
Old Greymuzzle? She's been the terror of the downs since I was a girl. And you just walked up and... well.

My husband's pin. He'd want someone brave to have it.

quests.title: The Still Wheel
quests.offer:
My wheel's stopped. Not broken - stopped. Something's jammed the race, and every time I clear it, it's jammed again by morning.

It's the sprites. Little blue things from the river, all giggling. Will you [clear the race]? And if you find the pin they stole off the wheel, I'll owe you a sack of flour.
quests.summary: River sprites keep jamming Bran the Miller's wheel outside Cotswold.

steps.goal: Chase the spritelings out of the reeds about 360 m south-east of Bran the Miller
Search the sprites' pool down the river

clue.name: a pool full of shiny things

steps.text: Buttons, a spoon, three thimbles - and Bran's iron wheel-pin, polished up like a jewel. Tiny wet footprints lead back upstream.

steps.goal: Deal with Thwori, the sprite who leads them, upstream on the west bank
steps.text: Thwori squeals and splashes away, and the other sprites follow. The race runs clear.

steps.goal: Bring the pin back to Bran
steps.say:
There she goes - hear that? That's the sound of bread.

Polished my pin, did they? Cheeky little beggars.

quests.title: Little Green Legs
quests.offer:
Half the harvest's in and the other half's walking off into the hills. Spriggarns. They come down at night, steal the sheaves and the sickles both, and dance on the stubble.

Will you [find the harvest]? Their rings are in the hills east of here. Bring back what you can - and make them think twice.
quests.summary: Spriggarns are stealing Cotswold's harvest and carrying it off to their rings in the hills.

steps.goal: Teach the spriggarns in the hills a lesson about 370 m east of Reeve Tobias
Search the spriggarn ring for the stolen sickles
steps.text: Sickles, a dozen, hung in a circle on a hawthorn like bells - and the sheaves trampled into a dancing floor.

steps.goal: Tell Reeve Tobias what you found
steps.say:
Dancing on it? Our bread? ...Brownies used to leave a sheaf out for the little folk at every harvest. My grandmother did. We stopped when the King died - there didn't seem much to thank anyone for.

Do we [leave a sheaf] out for them again, or [drive them off] for good?

options.say: A sheaf it is. One, at the edge of the field. And if they take a second, they'll hear from me.
Then we'll burn the hawthorn. They'll find somewhere else to dance.

gift.text: The little folk leave something on the doorstep the next morning.

quests.title: Ants in the Furrow
quests.offer:
Dragon ants. You've seen them? Big as dogs, and they've come over the ridge into my east field. They take the seed straight out of the furrow.

The workers I can live with. But somewhere up on the ridge there's a queen, and while she's laying there'll be no end of them. Will you [find the queen]?
quests.summary: Dragon ants from the eastern ridge are raiding Gronyr's farm.

steps.goal: Kill the dragon ant workers on the ridge about 410 m east of Gronyr the Farmer
Kill the dragon ant queen in her mound
steps.text: The queen goes down in a heap of legs. Her soldiers mill about, lost.

steps.goal: Tell Gronyr
steps.say: Gone? The queen? ...My grandfather's grandfather would've bought you a drink. I'll buy you two.

quests.title: The King's Deer
quests.offer:
The north woods were the King's own hunting. Nobody's said otherwise since he went - so the poachers decided nobody minds.

They've strung snares from the road to the heath. Will you [cut the snares]? And send the poachers home with a flea in their ear.
quests.summary: Poachers are snaring in the King's woods north of Cotswold.

steps.goal: Cut the poachers' snares by the north road about 70 m north-east of Forester Odo

clue.name: a wire snare in the bracken

steps.text: A snare, and another, and another - a dozen in a line. You cut them all.

steps.goal: Drive off the young poachers at their camp
Tell Forester Odo
steps.say: Cut, all of them? Good. Arthur's not here to mind his deer. So I mind them.

quests.title: Cutpurses on the King's Road
quests.offer:
The road from here to Camelot used to be the safest in Albion. Now a gang of cutpurses works it - children, half of them, and the other half ought to know better.

Last night they took the parish tithe from Brother Idris's boy. Will you [clear the road]? The gang camps in the hills east of the crossroads.
quests.summary: A gang of cutpurses robs travellers on the road to Camelot. They took the parish tithe.

steps.goal: Clear the cutpurses on the Camelot road about 270 m south-east of Warden Hollis
Break up the gang's camp in the hills
Defeat the gang's lieutenant
steps.text: The lieutenant falls. In his coat: the tithe purse - and a second purse, full of new silver.

stages.name: Hob Crowley
stages.announce: A broad man with a short sword steps out of the trees. 'That's my road, friend. My road, my tax.'

steps.goal: Return the tithe to Warden Hollis
steps.say:
The tithe, thank God. And this other purse... new silver, every coin. Stamped with a red seal I don't know.

Cutpurses don't carry new silver. Somebody's paying them.

quests.title: The Red Seal
quests.offer:
Hollis sent you with this purse? Good. Look at the seal - a red key under a crown. I've seen it twice: on a dead smuggler, and on a letter I wasn't meant to read.

The bandits on the eastern ridge have a hedge-wizard with them - a thaumaturge. If anyone keeps their accounts, it's him. Will you [find his accounts]?
quests.summary: Watch-Captain Elidyr of Prydwen Keep thinks the bandits are being paid - in silver stamped with a red seal.

steps.goal: Fight through the bandits on the eastern ridge about 700 m north-east of Watch-Captain Elidyr
Defeat the gang's thaumaturge
steps.text: The thaumaturge's satchel spills open: a ledger, in a neat hand.

stages.name: Hollin the Hexer
stages.announce: A thin man in a feathered cloak shrieks a curse and the air goes sour. 'Nobody reads my books!'

steps.goal: Read the thaumaturge's ledger

clue.name: a ledger in a neat hand

steps.text: 'Paid: to keep the Watch busy on the roads, forty marks. Paid: to keep away from the tomb on the eastern hill, twenty marks. Received of the Crimson, by the hand of the Warden of the Tomb.'

steps.goal: Bring the ledger to Watch-Captain Elidyr
steps.say:
'Keep the Watch busy on the roads.' So all this - the cutpurses, the robberies - it's a curtain. And behind it, the old Roman tomb on the eastern hill.

The Crimson. I don't know the name. I don't like it.

quests.title: The Old Fort
quests.offer:
The gang's master has a name now: Gamwell the Red-Handed, and he holds the old fort south of the river. Kill him and the curtain comes down.

He's no cutpurse - he fought at Camlann, they say, on the wrong side. Will you [take the fort]? Bring friends if you have them. I'll have men on the bridge.
quests.summary: Gamwell the Red-Handed, master of the Camelot Road Gang, holds the old fort south of the river.

steps.goal: Cross the river south of Prydwen Keep
steps.text: The bridge is held by Elidyr's men. Beyond it, on the hill, the old fort's walls - and smoke.

steps.goal: Fight into the old fort about 410 m south-east of Watch-Captain Elidyr
Defeat Gamwell the Red-Handed
steps.text: Gamwell goes down on one knee. 'Camlann,' he says, 'was the last honest fight I saw.' Then nothing.

stages.name: Gamwell the Red-Handed
stages.announce: A grey-bearded man in old mail draws a sword with a broken crown on the pommel. 'Mordred paid better than Arthur, and so does she.'

steps.goal: Report to Watch-Captain Elidyr
steps.say:
'So does she.' Not he. She.

The roads are ours again. And the curtain's down - so now we can see what's behind it on the eastern hill.

quests.title: Arthur's Huntsmen
quests.offer:
You've heard of the hunt for the Twrch Trwyth? The great boar - a king turned into a beast - that Arthur chased from Ireland across all Wales. Three of the huntsmen were brothers: Cilydd, Cyfer and Cyfwlch Difwych. Best hound-men in Albion.

After Camlann they didn't come home. They're in the eastern hills, with their hounds, and they kill anyone who comes near. Will you [find the brothers]? I want to know what they've become.
quests.summary: Sir Bedwyr of Prydwen Keep asks you to find the Difwych brothers, Arthur's huntsmen, who went wild after Camlann.

steps.goal: Kill the Difwych hounds in the eastern hills about 930 m north-east of Sir Bedwyr
Search the brothers' hunting camp

clue.name: a camp of skins and old spears

steps.text: Boar spears, all of them notched with the same mark - a boar's head. A map of Wales scratched on a hide, with a trail across it, and the trail goes round and round.

steps.goal: Face Cilydd Difwych
steps.text: Cilydd falls. 'The boar,' he says. 'We'll have him at the river. Tell Arthur.'

steps.goal: Tell Sir Bedwyr
steps.say:
Still hunting the boar. The Twrch Trwyth went into the sea off Cornwall years ago - Arthur let him go.

They never heard the hunt was over. No one ever came to tell them.

quests.title: The Hunt That Never Ended
quests.offer:
Cyfwlch was the eldest. He had Arthur's horn - the horn that called the hunt in and sent it out. If anyone can still reach them, it's that horn.

Take my word to him: the hunt is over, the King is gone, and the Round Table would have them back. Will you [take the word]? And if he won't hear it... do what you must.
quests.summary: Sir Bedwyr sends you to Cyfwlch Difwych, eldest of the brothers, with word that the hunt is over.

steps.goal: Get past Cyfer Difwych
steps.text: Cyfer drops his spear. 'Brother,' he calls. 'Brother, someone's come from Camelot.'

steps.goal: Face Cyfwlch Difwych, eldest of the brothers
steps.text: Cyfwlch sinks down against a stone, the old horn still on its cord round his neck.

steps.goal: Tell Sir Bedwyr how it ended
steps.say:
He wouldn't hear it. No. They never could hear anything but the hunt.

You have the horn? Then you have a choice. We can [blow the horn] - the old call that brings the hunt home - and let the hills hear it. Or [keep the horn] at Prydwen, and remember them the way they were.

options.say:
Then blow it. Long and low, the way Cyfwlch did.

...Hear the hounds? They've stopped. All over the hills. They've stopped.
Then it goes on the wall above the gate, and every knight who rides out will touch it for luck.

quests.title: Red Robes on the Hill
quests.offer:
I bless the dead in the barrow fields every Sunday. This spring, men in red robes started coming out of the old Roman tomb at night, and the dead started getting up.

I'm a priest, not a soldier. Will you [go to the tomb]? See who they are. Sage Tegid might know their sign.

topics.morgana: Arthur's half-sister. A healer once, they say - she was one of the queens who carried him to Avalon. And then something changed.

quests.summary: Men in red robes come out of Mithra's Tomb at night, and the dead of the barrow fields are walking.

steps.goal: Kill the red-robed acolytes at the tomb mouth about 360 m south-east of Brother Idris
steps.text: One acolyte carries a knife of black stone with a red-key hilt.

steps.goal: Show the knife to Sage Tegid
steps.say:
A red key under a crown. The Crimson. They're old - older than Arthur. They worshipped what lives under the hill, and they called it by a woman's name.

In my grandmother's day that name was [Morgana].

steps.goal: Tell Brother Idris
steps.say:
Morgana le Fay. The King's own sister. Under Camelot's nose, in a Roman tomb.

God help us. Well. He has so far.

quests.title: The Dead Won't Lie Still
quests.offer:
The rite raises them, Tegid says - the dead in the barrows answer the call from the tomb. There are three stones, marked with the red key, set in the barrow fields to carry the call.

Will you [break the stones]? And lay to rest whatever's guarding them.
quests.summary: Three rite stones in the barrow fields carry the Crimson's call to the dead. Brother Idris wants them broken.

steps.goal: Break the first rite stone about 190 m south of Brother Idris

clue.name: a stone marked with a red key

steps.text: The stone cracks down the middle, and the red key fades like a bruise.

steps.goal: Destroy the undead filidh guarding the barrow ring
Break the second rite stone

clue.name: a stone marked with a red key

steps.text: The second stone breaks. Somewhere under the hill, someone screams in anger.

steps.goal: Lay the rotting dead at the rite to rest
Break the third rite stone

clue.name: a stone marked with a red key

steps.text: The third stone splits, and every dead thing in the barrow fields falls down where it stands.

steps.goal: Tell Brother Idris
steps.say:
They've lain down. All of them. I'll bury them again on Sunday - properly.

The rite's broken. Whoever leads it will know.

quests.title: The Tomb-Warden
quests.offer:
The ledger named him - 'the Warden of the Tomb'. Brother Malgwyn, he calls himself. He was one of ours once, a brother of the Church.

He'll be at the tomb mouth with his best. You'll want friends. Will you [face the Warden]? Bring me whatever he carries.
quests.summary: Brother Malgwyn, Warden of the Tomb, leads the Crimson's rite at Mithra's Tomb.

steps.goal: Fight through the crimson initiates at the tomb mouth about 390 m south-east of Brother Idris
Defeat Brother Malgwyn, Warden of the Tomb
steps.text: Malgwyn falls across the tomb's threshold. A letter, sealed with the red key, slides out of his sleeve.

stages.name: Brother Malgwyn
stages.objective: Defeat Brother Malgwyn, Warden of the Tomb
stages.announce: A man in red robes over a monk's habit stands in the tomb mouth. 'The Lady keeps her promises. Do you know what she promised me? I'll show you.'

steps.goal: Read the letter in Malgwyn's sleeve

clue.name: a letter sealed with a red key

steps.text: 'Malgwyn - the Tomb is done with. Go north to the Bishop. The Mountains are ready, and the gate in the lake will open at midsummer. M.' The hand is fine, and the M is drawn like a crown.

steps.goal: Take the letter to Lady Enid at the camp below Darkness Falls
steps.say:
'Go north to the Bishop.' North of Camelot there is one bishop: Burhoff, of Vetusta Abbey, in the Black Mountains. A holy man, we're told.

And 'the gate in the lake'... The Round Table must see this. You've done Albion a service today, whatever comes of it.

default.text: From Lady Enid, in the Round Table's name.

quests.title: The Cracked Door
quests.offer:
The door to Darkness Falls is held. The Watch holds it. But it's cracked - demons come out round the edges, little ones at first, and every month bigger ones.

There's one at the mouth called Fielath. He's learned our names. Will you [hold the door] with us? Kill the manes that come out, and see Fielath off.
quests.summary: Demons are getting round the Watch at the mouth of Darkness Falls.

steps.goal: Kill the manes demons at Darkness Falls' mouth about 390 m east of Sir Barwick
See Fielath off
steps.text: Fielath bursts like a coal in a fire. 'BARCROFT,' it howls as it goes. 'BERWICK!'

steps.goal: Tell Sir Barwick
steps.say:
He called me Berwick? Even dying. Demons.

The door holds another month. Thank you.

quests.title: The Grove Below the River
quests.offer:
There's a grove of filidh on the south bank - the old singers, who kept the songs before the Church came. They kept Merlin's songs too, they say. They've always kept to themselves.

This spring they've started turning travellers away with spears. Their leader is a woman called Aithne Con. Will you [go to the grove]? I'd rather know why than fight them.
quests.summary: The filidh of the south bank have turned hostile. Lady Enid wants to know why.

steps.goal: Get past the filidh on the paths about 270 m south of Lady Enid
Face Aithne Con, who leads the grove
steps.text: Aithne Con lowers her staff. 'We sing what Merlin sang: when the King sleeps, the Lady wakes. She has woken. We will not let her singers through our grove.'

steps.goal: Tell Lady Enid what Aithne said
steps.say:
'When the King sleeps, the Lady wakes.' Morgana again. So the filidh aren't our enemies - they're guarding their grove against the Crimson.

Shall I [send them word] that the Watch stands with them? Or do we [leave them be]? They have no love for Camelot.

options.say: Then I'll send a knight with bread and no spears. Merlin's riddle came back with her answer: 'Where the thorn grows, the threads meet.' Campacorentin has a thorn.
Then they hold their grove and we hold our roads, and neither of us lets the Crimson pass.

quests.title: Cronker of the West Bank
quests.offer:
There's something on the west bank the cutpurses won't go near - a great brute the farmers call Cronker. It's been there longer than the Wardens have, and it's always kept to the river.

Now it's coming up into the fields at night. Will you [hunt Cronker]? Take friends. It doesn't go down easy.
quests.summary: The brute called Cronker has started coming up from the west bank into Cotswold's fields.

steps.goal: Find Cronker's trail on the west bank about 370 m south of Warden Hollis
steps.text: Prints the size of millstones, going south along the bank.

steps.goal: Kill Cronker
steps.text: Cronker crashes down in the shallows, and the river runs brown for an hour.

steps.goal: Tell Warden Hollis
steps.say:
Cronker. Dead. My father wouldn't believe it.

The Wardens owe you, friend. More than once now.
